lessons.trigger: When optimizing ERA5 regular-grid Zarr for tensor_loading.v1 full-field C,H,W reads.
lessons.recommendation: Use explicit sample-access-aligned chunks: one time sample and one selector plane per chunk, with the full selected latitude and longitude extents, while preserving all dimensions and channels.
lessons.scope: Regular-grid Zarr v3 pipelines with full-field tensor consumer workloads.
lessons.evidence: The feasible parent passed all constraints but measured 30.9009 consumer_samples_per_second with 197 chunk objects for 28 samples and 3 channels; the workload read shuffled full C,H,W tensors.
lessons.caveat: This trajectory contains no measured alternate layout, so the chunking recommendation is a plausible engineering hypothesis rather than proven causation.

lessons.trigger: When optimizing footprint for ERA5 regular-grid Zarr where diagnostics separate chunk and metadata bytes.
lessons.recommendation: Target explicit deterministic lossless compression of data chunks before metadata tweaks, because the measured footprint is almost entirely chunk payload. Keep semantic content and artifact declarations unchanged.
lessons.scope: Regular-grid Zarr v3 pipelines with decoded float32 ERA5 pressure-level arrays and consolidated metadata.
lessons.evidence: The feasible parent passed all hard constraints with output_bytes 175,189,531; diagnostics reported chunk_bytes 175,164,494 and metadata_bytes 25,037.
lessons.caveat: This identifies where bytes are concentrated in one trajectory; it does not prove that any specific compressor or level will reduce bytes on every fixture.

lessons.trigger: When switching a feasible ERA5 full-field tensor Zarr trajectory from footprint focus back to throughput focus.
lessons.recommendation: Keep the measured-correct sample-aligned full-spatial chunk layout, but bias explicit lossless codec choices toward read/decode speed rather than strong compression; avoid high compression levels selected mainly for output_bytes.
lessons.scope: Regular-grid Zarr v3 pipelines for shuffled full-field C,H,W tensor_loading.v1 reads over ERA5 pressure-level arrays.
lessons.evidence: The latest feasible parent passed all hard constraints with full-field chunks, consolidated Zarr v3, 91 chunk objects, and 62.0611 consumer_samples_per_second, but it used footprint-oriented Blosc-Zstd clevel 7. The prior archived node measured 52.9578 samples/s with a larger 197-object layout.
lessons.caveat: The measurements are single-run and confounded by multiple layout/codec changes, so they support a bounded engineering hypothesis rather than proving codec-level causation.

lessons.trigger: When optimizing throughput for ERA5 pressure-level Zarr full-field tensor reads after a Zstd-oriented or footprint-oriented feasible trajectory.
lessons.recommendation: Prefer the validated full-spatial sample-aligned chunks and avoid Zstd/high-compression data codecs for throughput; use either uncompressed chunks for a bounded throughput trial or a read-speed-biased lossless LZ4-style codec if compression is needed.
lessons.scope: Regular-grid consolidated Zarr v3 pipelines for ERA5 pressure-level tensor_loading.v1 shuffled C,H,W reads.
lessons.evidence: Feasible LZ4/read-speed-biased trajectories measured 77.7741 and 78.3523 consumer_samples_per_second with all hard constraints passing, while feasible Zstd-oriented trajectories in this supplied history measured 62.0611 and 55.3041 samples/s.
lessons.caveat: These are noisy single-run measurements with confounded prompt and implementation differences; they support a bounded engineering preference, not proof that codec choice alone caused the throughput differences.

lessons.trigger: When multiple requested ERA5 pressure-level channels share the same native source variable in a regular-grid Zarr tensor_loading.v1 workload.
lessons.recommendation: Consider grouping those channels into one native-variable data array with a real selected pressure_level dimension and selector chunk size 1, while declaring each field-selector channel separately in the artifact and including only requested selector values.
lessons.scope: ERA5 pressure-level consolidated Zarr v3 outputs with full-field C,H,W tensor reads and unambiguous channel selector declarations.
lessons.evidence: A feasible grouped uncompressed trajectory measured 174.2767 samples/s and 348,890,561 bytes versus the ungrouped uncompressed parent at 169.7737 samples/s and 348,895,698 bytes; a grouped Zstd9 trajectory also measured slightly fewer bytes than its ungrouped Zstd9 parent.
lessons.caveat: These are noisy single-run comparisons and grouping is confounded with implementation details; they support a bounded engineering preference, not proof that grouping alone caused the changes.

lessons.trigger: When optimizing throughput only for ERA5 pressure-level Zarr full-field tensor reads after a grouped uncompressed same-native-variable layout.
lessons.recommendation: Consider a bounded trial with one uncompressed sample-aligned full-spatial data array per requested field-selector channel, retaining a real selector dimension of length one and explicit artifact selector paths, instead of grouping same-native-variable pressure levels.
lessons.scope: Regular-grid consolidated Zarr v3 ERA5 pressure-level pipelines for shuffled tensor_loading.v1 C,H,W full-field reads.
lessons.evidence: The grouped uncompressed parent p016 passed all hard constraints with 178.8709 samples/s and 348,891,177 bytes. A feasible uncompressed throughput node p017 also passed all hard constraints and measured 184.3516 samples/s with 348,898,641 bytes.
lessons.caveat: These are noisy single-run measurements and p017 is confounded by implementation details; they support a bounded throughput hypothesis, not proof that ungrouping caused the higher measured rate.
